slot.brief: Give the mass of a compound produced from a given mass of a reactant with excess of the other reactant (simple mass-to-mass stoichiometry using molar masses).

stem: $5.4$ g of aluminium is heated in excess chlorine gas: $$2\text{Al} + 3\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{AlCl}_3$$ What mass of $\text{AlCl}_3$ is formed? (Atomic masses: Al $= 27$, Cl $= 35.5$)

verdicts.working:
Moles of Al = 5.4 g / 27 g/mol = 0.2 mol.
From stoichiometry, 2 mol of Al yields 2 mol of AlCl3, so moles of AlCl3 = 0.2 mol.
Molar mass of AlCl3 = 27 + 3 * 35.5 = 133.5 g/mol.
Mass of AlCl3 = 0.2 mol * 133.5 g/mol = 26.7 g.

working:
Moles of Al $= \dfrac{5.4}{27} = 0.2$ mol.
From $2\text{Al} : 2\text{AlCl}_3$, moles of $\text{AlCl}_3 = 0.2$ mol.
Molar mass of $\text{AlCl}_3 = 27 + 3(35.5) = 133.5$ g mol$^{-1}$.
Mass of $\text{AlCl}_3 = 0.2 \times 133.5 = 26.7$ g.

Independent check: Moles of Al = 5.4 g / 27 g/mol = 0.2 mol.
From stoichiometry, 2 mol of Al yields 2 mol of AlCl3, so moles of AlCl3 = 0.2 mol.

solution:
Al is limiting since Cl$_2$ is in excess. $n_{\text{Al}} = \dfrac{5.4}{27} = 0.2$ mol.
From $2\text{Al} \rightarrow 2\text{AlCl}_3$, $n_{\text{AlCl}_3} = 0.2$ mol.
$M(\text{AlCl}_3) = 27 + 3(35.5) = 133.5$ g/mol.
$$m = 0.2 \times 133.5 = 26.7\ \text{g}$$

draft.distractor_notes:
A ($13.35$ g): wrong mole ratio. The student takes 1 mol of $\text{AlCl}_3$ per 2 mol of Al and halves the moles.
B ($21.3$ g): partial answer. This is the mass of $\text{Cl}_2$ consumed ($0.3 \times 71$), not the mass of product.
D ($53.4$ g): the student uses the dimer $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$ molar mass ($267$) with $0.2$ mol, which doubles the answer.
